Six dashboards, built from the unified warehouse marts as fully static Plotly
pages — no server, no live compute, nothing to break. Each panel is tagged
with the audit question it answers; the full question-by-question checklist
(nine questions, each unanswerable or wrong from any single silo) lives in the
[silo audit memo](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/blob/main/docs/silo_audit.md).

Every frame below is the real artifact, embedded as-is; the source build is
[analysis/dashboards](https://github.com/JordanBeary/tributary/tree/main/analysis/dashboards).

## 1. Before and after: the silo audit

What each silo believed alone versus what the unified view shows — headcount
by system versus resolved consumers, and paid-channel ROI where the
click-value ranking inverts once revenue is joined through the auction.

## 2. The full funnel

Message → application → auction → sale → funded loan in one view: stage
volumes, stage-to-stage conversion by acquisition channel, and funded rate by
tier and clearing-price band. 12.7% of sold leads fund, declining from 14.3%
in tier 1 to 8.5% in tier 6.

<iframe class="dashboard-frame" data-src="embedded/02_full_funnel.html" title="Full funnel dashboard" loading="lazy"></iframe>

[Open full page](embedded/02_full_funnel.html){target="_blank"}

## 3. Auction economics

Earnings per lead offered by tier and FICO band, clearing-price spreads,
sell-through against floors, and buyer concentration (revenue-share HHI) by
tier. Tier-1 leads clear at a mean near $255; recent repeat applicants clear
at 0.52–0.75x fresh prices.

<iframe class="dashboard-frame" data-src="embedded/03_auction_economics.html" title="Auction economics dashboard" loading="lazy"></iframe>

[Open full page](embedded/03_auction_economics.html){target="_blank"}

## 4. Consumer identity

The identity story quantified: 2.40M auction lead ids and 2.28M CRM lead ids
resolve to 635,579 consumers; 69% of applications are repeats; 112,035
orphaned applications restored from the lake; and $12.0M of buyer spend on
consumers already bought within 30 days.

<iframe class="dashboard-frame" data-src="embedded/04_consumer_identity.html" title="Consumer identity dashboard" loading="lazy"></iframe>

[Open full page](embedded/04_consumer_identity.html){target="_blank"}

## 5. Marketing attribution

Revenue by channel through the auction — 93% of $209.2M attributable to a
marketing contact, $104.5M to paid channels, ROAS from 0.94x (display, below
break-even) to 3.06x (affiliate) — plus acquisition cost and last-touch
campaign coverage.

<iframe class="dashboard-frame" data-src="embedded/05_marketing_attribution.html" title="Marketing attribution dashboard" loading="lazy"></iframe>

[Open full page](embedded/05_marketing_attribution.html){target="_blank"}

## 6. The uplift experiment

The nurture-campaign holdout, read honestly: +0.109pp application lift
against an injected +0.115pp ground truth, with a confidence interval
spanning zero — the experiment is underpowered for the pooled effect at this
scale, and the dashboard says so rather than torturing significance out of
it.

<iframe class="dashboard-frame" data-src="embedded/06_uplift_experiment.html" title="Uplift experiment dashboard" loading="lazy"></iframe>

```{=html}
<script>
// Load each dashboard iframe only as it approaches the viewport. Six eager
// frames each pull their own copy of plotly.js; deferring to scroll keeps
// initial load light while the "Open full page" links remain the no-JS path.
(function () {
  var frames = document.querySelectorAll("iframe[data-src]");
  if (!("IntersectionObserver" in window)) {
    frames.forEach(function (f) { f.src = f.dataset.src; });
    return;
  }
  var io = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
    entries.forEach(function (e) {
      if (e.isIntersecting) {
        e.target.src = e.target.dataset.src;
        io.unobserve(e.target);
      }
    });
  }, { rootMargin: "200px" });
  // Arm on first interaction: nothing heavy loads until the visitor starts
  // reading (any scroll, tap, or keypress), then frames stream in as they
  // approach the viewport.
  var armed = false;
  function arm() {
    if (armed) return;
    armed = true;
    frames.forEach(function (f) { io.observe(f); });
  }
  ["scroll", "pointerdown", "keydown", "touchstart"].forEach(function (ev) {
    window.addEventListener(ev, arm, { once: true, passive: true });
  });
})();
</script>
```
